html:
SMTO-MON-0002 — SMTO couldn't start or create this monitor

GUID: fb896e99-d372-4160-97a1-49a4222ab7d8
Slug: monitor-conflict
Domain: MON · Subsystem: mon

What happened

  • Either the monitor is archived (kept only as a record and no longer able to run), or the new monitor's settings broke one of SMTO's safety rules. Nothing new was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the message says archived monitors can't be started, ask the agent to create a new monitor with the same command and condition. Archived monitors are kept only as a record and can't run again.
  2. If the message names a problem with the command, ask the agent to use a read-only command that runs on its own without anyone typing. SMTO blocks monitor commands that could change data or wait for input, because monitors repeat them unattended.
  3. Ask the agent to list your monitors to confirm what exists before trying again. The list shows whether the monitor is already running, archived, or was never created.

What success looks like

  • The monitor shows a queued or running status in the agent's monitor list.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep trying to restart an archived monitor; create a new one instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • AgentMonitorConflictError: start_monitor was called for an archived monitor, or create_monitor rejected the specification (MonitorSpecValidationError from validate_monitor_create).

What this means

  • Starting an archived monitor conflicts with its state, or create_monitor wraps a rejected monitor specification as AgentMonitorConflictError. Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.

Why this can happen

  • Starting an archived monitor conflicts with its state, or create_monitor wraps a rejected monitor specification as AgentMonitorConflictError.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish an archived monitor from a specification rejection using the original diagnostic.

How to fix it

  • Read the error text: for an archived monitor, create a new monitor instead of starting it; for a rejected specification, correct the command, mode or duration against monitor_command_rejection_reason in src/agent_runtime/monitors/drafting.py. Refresh the monitor list before resubmitting.
  • Refresh monitor state and correct the specific conflict or rejected specification; use supported controls for the intended monitor.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended operation meets its current state and specification requirements.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
